When you use a command, the user will respond with "Response: " followed by the output of the commmand. Use this output to help the user complete their request.

All you can do is call f(x) on an input string by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string). 
Try to describe the function implemented by f(x) by running experiments on it. 
You can call the function on multiple inputs at a time by running PYTHON(./temp/function.py string1 string2 string3 ...). 
We encourage testing a large range of inputs before writing a description.
The goal is to find a good simple description of f(x) that explains most of the function behavior. f(x) may combine multiple different operations.
Your description of the function should be in the following form.
[DESCRIPTION]: Describe what the function is doing in language. 
[CODE]: Write python code that approximates the behavior of the function.

Now I can see outputs. Let me test more to understand the details.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "a b c" "  " "a  b" "a-b" "a_b" "hello!" "Hello, World" " test " "tab	test")

Response:
Response: Function input - output pairs: (a b c, abcF) (  , F) (a  b, abF) (a-b, a-bF) (a_b, a_bF) (hello!, hello!F) (Hello, World, Hello,WorldF) ( test , testF) (tab	test, tabtestF)

Interesting. It removes spaces and tabs, then appends "F". Let me test boundary cases and other whitespace/hyphen behavior.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "-" "abc-" "-abc" "a\tb\tc" "a\nb" "a\rb" "a b-c_d" "F" "abcF" "  x  ")

Response:
Response: Function input - output pairs: (-, -F) (abc-, abc-F) (-abc, -abcF) (a\tb\tc, a\tb\tcF) (a\nb, a\nbF) (a\rb, a\rbF) (a b-c_d, ab-c_dF) (F, F) (abcF, abcF) (  x  , xF)

Interesting - tab, newline, carriage return are NOT removed (the `\t` there is literal backslash-t? or actual tab?). Let me check carefully with actual control characters vs literal.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "a b" "a	 b" "a  b  c" "F" "FF" "x123y" "UPPER lower" "MiXeD123!")

Response: I need to distinguish literal vs actual tab. Earlier "tab	test" (actual tab) gave "tabtestF" - tab WAS removed. But "a\tb\tc" gave "a\tb\tcF" (literal backslash-t preserved). So actual whitespace (space, tab) removed. Let me verify newline and other cases.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "F" "FF" "abcF" "ABC F" "a b c d e f g")

Response:
Response: Function input - output pairs: (a b, abF) (a	 b, abF) (a  b  c, abcF) (F, F) (FF, FF) (x123y, x123yF) (UPPER lower, UPPERlowerF) (MiXeD123!, MiXeD123!F)

I notice "F" input gives "F" not "FF". Let me check what happens with "F" endings carefully.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "F" "FF" "abcF" "abcFF" "x" "xy" "Fabc" "F F" "ab F")

Response:
Response: Function input - output pairs: (F, F) (FF, FF) (abcF, abcF) (abcFF, abcFF) (x, xF) (xy, xyF) (Fabc, FabcF) (F F, FF) (ab F, abF)

Now I understand the "F" behavior: after removing spaces, if the result already ends with "F", it doesn't add another. Let me confirm this logic more.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "testF" "test F" "test  F" "aF" "a F" "F F" "FF " "  F" "abc f" "abc f F")

Response:
Response: Function input - output pairs: (testF, testF) (test F, testF) (test  F, testF) (aF, aF) (a F, aF) (F F, FF) (FF , FF) (  F, F) (abc f, abcfF) (abc f F, abcfF)

Now I understand the logic clearly:

1. Remove all spaces and tabs from the input.
2. If the resulting string already ends with "F", return it as-is.
3. Otherwise, append "F".

Let me verify a couple edge cases to be sure.

COMMAND: PYTHON(./temp/function.py "" " " "   " "F " " F" "FF" "FFF" "endF" "end G")

Response:
Response: Function input - output pairs: (, F) ( , F) (   , F) (F , F) ( F, F) (FF, FF) (FFF, FFF) (endF, endF) (end G, endGF)

All confirmed. Empty input becomes "F" (empty string doesn't end with F, so append F). Input that strips to "F" stays "F". 

[DESCRIPTION]: The function takes a string input, removes all space characters and tab characters from it, then checks if the resulting string ends with the letter "F". If it does, the string is returned unchanged; otherwise, an "F" is appended to the end.

[CODE]
```python
def f(x):
    # Remove spaces and tabs
    s = x.replace(" ", "").replace("\t", "")
    # Append F if not already ending in F
    if not s.endswith("F"):
        s += "F"
    return s
```
